data: Baikonur's Proton complex: Proton 1, Salyut 1, Mir and ISS modules, Mars and Luna probes

Facts from the Wikipedia articles on Baikonur Cosmodrome Site 81 and the lists of Proton launches, and Encyclopedia Astronautica's Baikonur LC81/23 and LC81/24 pages. Coordinates are the site position on English Wikipedia (46.0708, 62.9847). Site 81 has two pads, 81/23 (now inactive) and 81/24, used with Site 200 by Proton.
Proton launch vehicle — International Launch Services

Site 81 is the Proton complex at Baikonur Cosmodrome, with two pads, 81/23 and 81/24, used alongside Site 200. Pad 23 saw the first Proton launch, Proton 1, on 16 July 1965. It also launched Mars 3, Luna 16, 17, 21 and 24, the Spektr and Priroda modules of Mir, and the Zarya (20 November 1998) and Zvezda (12 July 2000) modules of the International Space Station. Pad 24 launched Mars 2, 5 and 7, Venera 9, 10 and 12, and the Salyut stations 1, 4 and 6; Salyut 2, 3 and 5 went from pad 23. In 2013 a Proton-M crashed beside pad 24 just after lift-off. Pad 23 is inactive; pad 24 flew Elektro-L No. 5 on 12 February 2026, the final Proton-M in the DM-03 configuration.
